newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU member states divided on olive oil reforms.
newsitem.headline: EU member states divided on olive oil reforms.

text.p: European Union member states were split between north and south at a meeting of the special agriculture committee on Tuesday, over reform of the bloc's olive oil regime, an EU member state official said on Wednesday.
The outcome of the meeting between member state officials indicates there is unlikely to be any progress on the issue at the next farm minister's meeting on April 21, the official said.
Two weeks ago Spain's agriculture minister told state radio Mediterranean countries should remain united to block the reform.
"That appears to be the picture, with Spain leading a united bloc of producing countries against a solid bloc of non-producing countries who want reform," the official told Reuters.
The Commission presented a consultation paper at last month's farm council which outlined two alternatives for reform aimed at cutting forecast future overproduction and fraud.
The olive oil regime cost the EU 1.8 billion Ecus last year and the Commission is struggling to control subsidy fraud put at 10 times that of the cereal and other crop sectors.
The current regime offers production subsidies to small and large producers at different rates, said to be the main cause of widespread fraud.
The Commission says the regime should either be replaced with a system based on the number of trees and historic regional yields or changed to a single subsidy system.

"Spain and the rest of the producer countries discount fraud and the Commission's forecast of future over production. It is clear that they would like to continue with the present system while non-producers take the opposite view," the official said. --Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
